Vladislav Krasnopolski, son of Valentina and Vladimir, was born in Ukraine on Thursday, 5 Kislev 5747 (7 December 1986). He was the brother of Vitaly. When he arrived, a great light filled the family. His mother cared for him and devoted all her time to him, and from her he absorbed Zionist values, knowledge and wisdom.

Vladislav, known to those who loved him as Vladi, began his studies at an elementary school in his hometown in Ukraine. When he was ten, in the winter of 1996, he immigrated to Israel with his family. The family settled in Rishon LeZion, and Vladi entered the municipal school "Mekif Heh" in the city, where he studied in middle school and high school. He was a good student. He quickly picked up the Hebrew language, invested in his homework, and fulfilled every task assigned to him to the best of his ability.

Vladi was a quiet, modest boy who loved his family very much and was devoted to his parents. Although he was serious by nature, he loved to laugh and tell jokes. He was surrounded by friends who loved him, and he spent much time playing soccer with them and socializing.

At the age of seven, Vladi began training in judo. The sport became part of his way of life, and until his enlistment he trained and took part in competitions. His coach foresaw a great future for him in the discipline and believed that if Vladi did not enlist in the army, he could devote all his time to judo and advance. But Vladi thought otherwise. It was clear to him that he would enlist and contribute to the army and the state, and he aspired to serve as a combat soldier.

Vladislav enlisted in the Navy on 17 July 2005 and served in Flotilla 3, the missile boat flotilla, on the INS Hetz. His commanders valued his good qualities and testified that he was devoted to his role and to his friends.

Corporal Vladislav Krasnopolski fell while carrying out his duties on Thursday, 5 Tishrei 5767 (27 September 2006), at the age of nineteen. He was laid to rest in the military cemetery in Holon. He is survived by his parents and his brother.
